research_scope: Source-free independent Wave2 source-context mathematical prerequisite consolidation; original mathematical texts, human certification, missing-definition research and gate untouched.

aliases.reason: The total-quotient-ring source localizes R at the set S of its non-zero-divisors. This S contains 1 and is multiplicatively closed, exactly the general multiplicative-subset prerequisite used by ring/module localization. Requiring S to be all regular elements, rather than an arbitrary multiplicative subset, remains source-specific and is not generalized.

The topology-subbasis source forms finite intersections of open subbasic sets, including the empty finite intersection X. The independent topological-space axiom source uses the identical finite-indexed set-intersection operation with the same empty-index convention. Openness of each member, closure under intersections and basis generation are parent-specific, not intrinsic to a set intersection.

The affine-scheme-fibre-product formulation uses B⊗_A C of two commutative A-algebras, with multiplication (b⊗c)(b′⊗c′)=bb′⊗cc′. The universal-homeomorphism and syntomic sources use S⊗_R R′ with the same multiplication after renaming A=R, B=S, C=R′. This aliases the tensor-product algebra prerequisite only; no fibre-product universal property or homeomorphism/local-CI condition is equated.

The geometrically integral algebra source uses commutative unital scalar extension A⊗_k K for a field extension K/k, with exactly the same tensor-product K-algebra multiplication and canonical scalar structure as the previously consolidated R⊗_k K prerequisite (A and R are variable labels). The geometric integrality test and universal quantifier over K stay parent-specific.

The two independently sourced normal-subgroup formulations use gNg⁻¹={gng⁻¹:n∈N}. When N is a subgroup the conjugate subset is also a subgroup; the elementwise conjugation set operation is identical in both. Subgroup hypotheses, gNg⁻¹⊆N and equality/normality remain with each source, not inferred from arbitrary subset conjugation.
